minutes.headline: Planning Board ordered a traffic peer review of the Lunenburg Central warehouse and approved the 7-Eleven site plan.
minutes.summary: The board heard an informal request to put four homes on one lot at 733 Mass Ave, and members said the bylaw does not support it. Most of the night went to the Lunenburg Central warehouse on Leominster-Shirley Road, where abutters raised noise, lighting and traffic concerns. The board ordered a traffic peer review and continued that hearing, approved the 7-Eleven site plan with added conditions, approved a Water District sign change, and discussed how to fund the master plan.

public_comment.topic: Resident on Lake Shirley: noise from backup beepers, a noise barrier, Blanding's turtles, and effects on home values near the Lunenburg Central warehouse.
Resident on Robs Hill Road: overnight noise and the risk of traffic cutting through Robs Hill Road.
Closest abutter: noise, blind corner at Reservoir Road, unknown tenant and hours.
Resident asking about high-bay use, parking, truck routes, and whether the developer will build and hold or flip.
Follow-up on noise and its effect on real estate values and taxes around Lake Shirley.
Asked about dark-sky lighting and the stars.

votes.motion: Continue the 101 Pleasant Street hearing to September 27.
Continue the 97 and 125 Cross Street and 430 and 440 Mohawk Road hearing to September 27.
Continue the 360 Flat Hill Road hearings to the 27th.
Approve the ANR plan for 1263 Reservoir Road and 435 Leominster-Shirley Road. Discussion followed and endorsement was instead given an extension.
Require a peer review of the traffic study for 1263 Reservoir Road and 435 Leominster-Shirley Road.
Continue the 1263 Reservoir Road and 435 Leominster-Shirley Road hearing to September 27, 2021.
Approve the stormwater permit and site plan approval for 7-Eleven, Massachusetts Ave.
Approve the de minimis change for the Lunenburg Water District sign at 496 Massachusetts Ave.
Approve the minutes of 8/23/2021 for all hearings.

budget_items.what_was_said: The master plan RFP drew no bids and bidders said the money was too little. Members debated going through capital planning versus a standalone town meeting article.
MRPC is applying for a competitive grant to evaluate areas for industrial zoning. Part of the local match would come from DLTA funds.
Recalled earlier funding for the renovation study and a later amount for a new-building study. Town meeting funding articles are being prepared.

decisions.decision: Chair granted an extension of time to endorse the ANR plan for the Lunenburg Central lot to September 30 so staff can consult the building inspector about the easement and frontage.
Applicant will return in a few weeks with answers on the warehouse concerns; the traffic peer review will be done through the board's engineer.
Planning director will ask MRPC about the master plan RFP and check costs; the funding route is left open.
A public hearing will be scheduled in October on a limited business district dimensional table change.
Staff to draft a Water District watershed protection district article for the next meeting.

what_happened.line: The board voted to require a peer review of the traffic study for the Lunenburg Central warehouse and continued that hearing to September 27, 2021.
A motion to approve the 7-Eleven stormwater permit and site plan was made after discussion of added conditions; the outcome is not audible in the recording.
The chair granted an extension to September 30 to endorse the ANR plan for the Lunenburg Central lot, so staff can consult the building inspector on the easement and frontage.
Abutters and residents raised noise, lighting, truck traffic and cut-through concerns about the warehouse during public comment.
The board approved a de minimis sign change for the Lunenburg Water District at 496 Massachusetts Ave.

why_it_matters: The warehouse is the largest pending project on the board's agenda, and the traffic peer review gives neighbors an independent check before the board decides on noise, hours and truck routes.
The master plan request drew no bids and the funding route is undecided, so residents may be asked to vote on money for it at a town meeting.
watch_next: The September 27, 2021 continued hearings, including the Lunenburg Central warehouse and the traffic peer review.
A public hearing in October on the limited business district dimensional table change, and the Water District watershed protection article at the next meeting.
